info.title: MOCO API v1 (beta)
info.description:
Official API documentation for MOCO API v1.

## General

- Request payloads to MOCO must be sent as valid JSON with a mandatory `Content-Type: application/json` header. Responses are also sent as JSON.
- All requests have to be authenticated with an API key.
- Example responses showcase the happy case, i.e. usually the `200 OK` response.
- Collections are usually paginated.
- Zapier triggers are **not** triggered for API requests.
- Timestamps `created_at` and `updated_at` are sent for all entities in UTC, as ISO8601 format.
- For synchronization almost all resources can be filtered by `updated_after` passing a time in UTC, as ISO8601 format.

## Authentication

There are two ways to authenticate against MOCO:

1. **User API key**. Can be found under the "Integrations" tab on the profile page.
2. **Account API key**. Has to be created in Settings > Extensions > API & Webhooks, with either read-only or full access on all endpoints.

Both kinds of keys are provided as an Authorization header. See the security schemes below for supported formats.

## Impersonation

By default all requests are scoped to the authenticated user. Some resources cannot be provided with a `user_id` or similar, like `Activities` and `User Presences`. This reflects the behaviour in the UI, since every user can only create their own activities or presences. But you can login as another user provided that the authenticated user has permission to *Staff*. To achieve the same behaviour in the API, set the following header: `X-IMPERSONATE-USER-ID: 123` (user id to act on behalf of).

## Rate Limiting

You can expect to be able to send 120 requests per 2 minutes (~1 request per second). For the unlimited plan, it is 1200 requests per 2 minutes (~10 per second). If you exceed this limit, the server responds with `429 Too Many Requests`.

## Pagination

Responses are paginated with a common default of 100 entries per page. In the HTTP response header, the current page, the entries per page and the number of total entries is reported. There is also a `Link` header with links to the consecutive page.

- **X-Page** – current page number
- **X-Per-Page** – number of entries per page
- **X-Total** – total number of records
- **Link** – `<https://{account}.mocoapp.com/api/v1/projects?page=4>; rel="next"`

If there is no Link header with `rel="next"`, the current page is the last page.

## Sorting

Sorting is controlled by the `sort_by` query parameter. Its value is the field name that should be sorted, followed by an optional sorting order (`asc` or `desc`, default is `asc`).

Example: `https://{account}.mocoapp.com/api/v1/offers?sort_by=title desc`

## Errors and HTTP Status Codes

The MOCO API is mostly conformant with the general HTTP status codes.

Here are the most common errors you will see:

- **401 Unauthorized** – Check the error message in the response body.
- **403 Forbidden** – Check your Authentication or your MOCO user permission.
- **404 Not Found** – Check that the resource exists (maybe it was deleted in the meantime).
- **422 Unprocessable Entity** – Check the provided error message in the response body.
- **429 Too Many Requests** – Check the Rate Limiting section above.

## Custom Fields

Many resources support custom fields, which must first be defined in the MOCO settings. They are readable and writable via the `custom_properties` field, keyed by the custom field name:

```json
"custom_properties": {
  "UID": "123-UID-456",
  "Line of business": "Automotive"
}
```

Writing custom fields:

- Unknown custom field names are silently ignored.
- The provided custom fields are merged with the existing ones: only the submitted keys are updated, all others stay unchanged. Keys cannot be removed via the API.
- The total size of all custom field values of a record is limited to 12 kB; exceeding it fails with `422 Unprocessable Entity`.
- Values that do not match the configured options of `Select`/`MultiSelect` fields are ignored.

All values are encoded as strings, except `MultiSelect`, which is encoded as an array:

- **String / Textarea** – `"Automotive"`
- **Link** – `"https://www.example.com"` (must be a valid URL with scheme `http`, `https`, `mailto` or `tel`)
- **Date** – `"2021-12-31"` (strict format `YYYY-MM-DD`)
- **Boolean** – `"0"` (No) or `"1"` (Yes)
- **Select** – `"Value"`
- **MultiSelect** – `["Value 1", "Value 2"]`

For filtering records by custom field values, see the `custom_properties` query parameter of the respective list endpoints.

## WebHooks

WebHook subscriptions are managed via the `/account/web_hooks` endpoints. Whenever a subscribed event occurs, MOCO sends an HTTPS `POST` request with the affected record as JSON payload to the configured URL.

Deliveries include the following headers:

- **X-Moco-Target** – record type, e.g. `Activity`, `Company`, `Project`
- **X-Moco-Event** – `create`, `update` or `delete` (bookkeeping exports support `create` and `delete` only)
- **X-Moco-Timestamp** – event timestamp in milliseconds
- **X-Moco-Signature** – HMAC signature of the payload, see below
- **X-Moco-User-Id** – ID of the user that triggered the event
- **X-Moco-Account-Url** – account subdomain
- **X-Moco-Origin** – `api` if the change was made via the API, otherwise empty

Please note:

- Deliveries are asynchronous and not guaranteed to arrive in order; use the timestamp header if ordering matters.
- The receiver has to respond within 10 seconds with a 2xx status code. Other responses, timeouts and connection errors count as failures and are retried with exponential backoff.
- After 50 consecutive failures the account owner is notified by email; after 500 consecutive failures the WebHook is disabled automatically (a successful delivery resets the counter).
- Payloads of `delete` events only contain the record `id` (plus `custom_properties`, where supported).

### Signature verification

`X-Moco-Signature` is the hex digest of an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body, signed with the 32-character hexadecimal key displayed in the WebHook overview (Settings › Extensions › API & Webhooks).

Ruby:

```ruby
signature = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest("SHA256", signature_key, raw_request_body)
```

NodeJS:

```javascript
const signature = require("crypto").createHmac("sha256", signatureKey).update(rawRequestBody).digest("hex")
```

OpenSSL CLI:

```bash
echo -n '{"id":111}' | openssl sha256 -hmac "1d608b9d72219b90ff2393a1d3ee0ac0"
```

tags.name: AccountCatalogServices
tags.description:
Account-level catalog of reusable service definitions.

<sub>Synonyme: Katalog, Leistungskatalog</sub>

tags.name: AccountCustomProperties
tags.description:
Custom fields configurable per account for extending entity data.

<sub>Synonyme: Eigene Felder</sub>

tags.name: AccountExpenseTemplates
tags.description:
Reusable templates for recurring expense entries.

<sub>Synonyme: Standard-Zusatzleistungen, Artikel</sub>

tags.description:
Hourly rates configured at the account level.

<sub>Synonyme: Stundensätze, interne Stundensätze</sub>

tags.name: AccountTaskTemplates
tags.description:
Reusable task templates available across projects.

<sub>Synonyme: Standardleistungen</sub>

tags.name: AccountWebHooks
tags.description:
Webhook subscriptions for receiving real-time event notifications.

<sub>Synonyme: Automatisierung</sub>

tags.name: Activities
tags.description:
Time tracking entries. Activities are always created for the user the API key belongs to; use impersonation to create for other users. `seconds` are the billable seconds; `worked_seconds` are the seconds counted towards the user's actual hours. A timer can only be running on one activity at a time per user.

<sub>Synonyme: Zeiterfassung, Projektzeit, Zeiteintrag, Zeiteinträge</sub>

tags.name: Comments
tags.description:
Notes on entities. Text accepts plain text or HTML; all tags except `div`, `strong`, `em`, `u`, `pre`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `br` are stripped. Only manually created comments can be deleted via the API.

<sub>Synonyme: Kommentare, Nachrichten</sub>

tags.name: Companies
tags.description:
Customers, suppliers, and organizations. Type can be `customer`, `supplier`, or `organization`. For `custom_properties` filtering, the `type` parameter must be provided.

<sub>Synonyme: Firmen, Kunden, Lieferanten, Andere Firmen</sub>

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description:
Contact persons associated with companies.

<sub>Synonyme: Kontakte, Ansprechpersonen</sub>

tags.name: Contracts
tags.description:
Contracts and service agreements with customers or suppliers.

<sub>Synonyme: Projektzuweisungen</sub>

tags.name: DealCategories
tags.description:
Categories for classifying sales leads and deals.

<sub>Synonyme: Akquise-Stufen, Lead-Stufen</sub>

tags.name: Deals
tags.description:
Sales leads. Company and person are optional. The category is only relevant when status is `pending`.

<sub>Synonyme: Leads, Akquise, Vertrieb</sub>

tags.name: Expenses
tags.description:
Expense entries billed to projects or customers.

<sub>Synonyme: Spesen, Auslagen, Reisekosten</sub>

tags.name: InvoiceAttachments
tags.description:
File attachments associated with invoices.

<sub>Synonyme: Rechnungsanhänge, Anhänge</sub>

tags.name: InvoiceBookkeepingExports
tags.description:
Bookkeeping exports for invoice data (e.g. DATEV).

<sub>Synonyme: Buchhaltungsexporte, Rechnungsexporte</sub>

tags.name: InvoicePayments
tags.description:
Payments recorded against invoices.

<sub>Synonyme: Zahlungen, Zahlungseingang</sub>

tags.name: InvoiceReminders
tags.description:
Payment reminders sent to customers for outstanding invoices.

<sub>Synonyme: Zahlungserinnerungen, Mahnungen</sub>

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description:
`reversed`/`reversal` boolean pair distinguishes canceled invoices from their cancellation invoices. `activity_hours_modified` indicates whether invoice positions no longer correspond to the timesheet. List responses omit detail fields (`salutation`, `footer`, `items`, `payments`, `reminders`).

<sub>Synonyme: Rechnungen, Ausgangsrechnungen, Abrechnung</sub>

tags.name: LetterPapers
tags.description:
Letter paper layouts used as backgrounds for invoices and offers.

<sub>Synonyme: Briefpapier, Vorlagen</sub>

tags.name: OfferAttachments
tags.description:
File attachments associated with offers.

<sub>Synonyme: Angebotsanhänge, Anhänge</sub>

tags.name: OfferConfirmations
tags.description:
Offer confirmations for accepted offers.

<sub>Synonyme: Auftragsbestätigung</sub>

tags.name: OfferCustomerApproval
tags.description:
Customer approval workflow for offers.

<sub>Synonyme: Angebotsbestätigung</sub>

tags.name: Offers
tags.description:
Quotes and proposals sent to customers.

<sub>Synonyme: Angebote, Kostenvoranschläge, Offerten</sub>

tags.name: PlanningEntries
tags.description:
Project and resource scheduling. Each entry references either a project or a deal (the other is `null`). Created for the requesting user unless `user_id` is supplied.

<sub>Synonyme: Planungseinträge, Planung</sub>

tags.name: PlannedPurchases
tags.description:
Planned purchases represent one-time or recurring planned purchases.
When `frequency` is `once`, the planned purchase is a single non-recurring
purchase. All other frequency values (`weekly`, `biweekly`, `monthly`,
`quarterly`, `biannual`, `annual`) create recurring planned purchases that
generate individual purchases at the specified interval until `finish_date`
is reached. Automatic purchase creation only occurs when the `net_total`
exceeds the account's recurring creation threshold; otherwise the
recurrence is tracked but no purchase is created.

The read-only `variant`
field reflects this: `once` for one-time, `recurring` for all others. When
`frequency` is set to `once`, `finish_date` is automatically cleared.

<sub>Synonyme: Geplante Ausgaben, wiederkehrende geplante Ausgaben</sub>

tags.name: Profile
tags.description:
The authenticated user's own profile data.

<sub>Synonyme: Profil, Benutzer</sub>

tags.name: ProjectGroups
tags.description:
Groups for organizing projects into categories or portfolios.

<sub>Synonyme: Projektgruppen</sub>

tags.name: ProjectPaymentSchedules
tags.description:
Payment schedules defining installments for project billing.

<sub>Synonyme: Abrechnungspläne</sub>

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
`hourly_rate` and `billing_variant` are linked: for `task` or `user` billing, `hourly_rate` becomes a mean value. `currency` cannot be changed after creation. For retainer projects, `start_date` must be the first day and `finish_date` the last day of a month.

<sub>Synonyme: Projekte, Jobs</sub>

tags.name: PurchaseBookkeepingExports
tags.description:
Bookkeeping exports for purchase/supplier invoice data (e.g. DATEV).

<sub>Synonyme: Buchhaltungsexporte, Ausgabenexporte</sub>

tags.name: PurchaseBudgets
tags.description:
Budget limits for purchase and expense tracking per project or category.

<sub>Synonyme: Ausgabenbudgets, Jahresbudgets</sub>

tags.name: PurchaseCategories
tags.description:
Categories for classifying supplier invoices and purchases.

<sub>Synonyme: Aufwandskategorien, Aufwände</sub>

tags.name: PurchaseDrafts
tags.description:
Purchase order definitions for recurring or one-time purchases with budget tracking.

<sub>Synonyme: Ausgabenentwürfe</sub>

tags.name: PurchasePayments
tags.description:
Payments recorded against supplier invoices.

<sub>Synonyme: Zahlungen, Zahlungsausgang</sub>

tags.name: Purchases
tags.description:
Supplier invoices and expenses. `status`: `pending` = Inbox, `archived` = Archive. `approval_status`: `none`, `approved`, `denied`, or `pending`. Item updates after creation are not supported via PUT/PATCH.

<sub>Synonyme: Ausgaben, Eingangsrechnungen</sub>

tags.name: Receipts
tags.description:
Expense receipts. When updating, providing `items` overwrites all existing items entirely; submit the complete array. Deletion is only possible before a refund request has been created.

<sub>Synonyme: Belege</sub>

tags.name: RecurringExpenses
tags.description:
Recurring expense entries billed at regular intervals.

<sub>Synonyme: Wiederkehrende Ausgaben</sub>

tags.name: RevenueCategories
tags.description:
Revenue categories for classifying tasks and expenses for accounting exports.

<sub>Synonyme: Erlöskategorien, Erlöse</sub>

tags.name: Reports
tags.description:
Aggregated reports for time, revenue, and project performance.

<sub>Synonyme: Berichte</sub>

tags.name: Schedules
tags.description:
Schedules are used for absences only. Use Planning Entries for project schedules. The schedule representation contains among the standard fields also: assignment (absence) and user (assigned staff).

<sub>Synonyme: Abwesenheiten, Urlaub, Absenzen</sub>

tags.name: Session
tags.description:
Authentication session management.

<sub>Synonyme: Sitzung</sub>

tags.name: Taggings
tags.description:
Associations between tags and entities.

<sub>Synonyme: Label</sub>

tags.name: Tags
tags.description:
Labels scoped to a `context`. The `context` and `color` cannot be changed after creation. Use `merge_tag_id` on delete to consolidate tags.

<sub>Synonyme: Label</sub>

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description:
Project tasks defining billable activities within a project.

<sub>Synonyme: Leistungen</sub>

tags.name: Todos
tags.description:
Actionable to-do items that can be assigned to users and attached to assignments or users.

<sub>Synonyme: Aufgaben, To-dos</sub>

tags.name: Units
tags.description:
Teams. Users are assigned to a unit by updating the user record with the `unit_id` attribute. Deletion is only possible if no users are assigned.

<sub>Synonyme: Teams, Abteilungen</sub>

tags.name: UserAbsenceRequests
tags.description:
Absence requests (vacation, sickness, other) submitted by users for approval.

<sub>Synonyme: Abwesenheitsanträge, Urlaubsanträge, Absenzanträge</sub>

tags.name: UserEmployments
tags.description:
Employment records defining working hours and contracts for users.

<sub>Synonyme: Wochenmodelle, Soll, Zeitkonto</sub>

tags.name: UserHolidays
tags.description:
Public and custom holidays configured per user or account.

<sub>Synonyme: Urlaub, Urlaubskonto</sub>

tags.name: UserPresences
tags.description:
Time clock entries recording actual presence hours of users.

<sub>Synonyme: Arbeitszeiten, Arbeitszeiterfassung</sub>

tags.name: UserRoles
tags.description:
Role-based permission sets assigned to users.

<sub>Synonyme: Benutzerrolle, Rollen, Zugriffsrechte</sub>

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
Staff members. Deletion is only possible if no hours have been billed. Employment records must be terminated separately via `/users/employments`.

<sub>Synonyme: Personen, Benutzer, Personal</sub>

tags.name: UserWorkTimeAdjustments
tags.description:
Manual adjustments to users' recorded work time.

<sub>Synonyme: Korrekturen, Zeitkonto</sub>

tags.name: VatCodePurchases
tags.description:
VAT codes applied to purchase/supplier invoices.

<sub>Synonyme: Steuercodes, Steuersätze, Vorsteuer</sub>

tags.name: VatCodeSales
tags.description:
VAT codes applied to sales invoices and offers.

<sub>Synonyme: Steuercodes, Steuersätze, Umsatzsteuer</sub>

TokenAuth.name: Authorization
TokenAuth.description:
API key as token auth header.
Supports user API keys and account API keys (read-only or full-access).
Example: Token token=YOUR_API_KEY

BearerAuth.description:
API key as Bearer token.
Supports user API keys and account API keys (read-only or full-access).
Example: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

ImpersonateUserId.name: X-IMPERSONATE-USER-ID
ImpersonateUserId.description:
Execute request on behalf of another user if the authenticated user has permission to *Staff*.
Some resources, such as Activities and User Presences, can be created for other users only if this header is used.

SortBy.name: sort_by
SortBy.description: Field and optional direction, e.g. `title desc`.

UpdatedAfter.name: updated_after
UpdatedAfter.description:
ISO 8601 UTC timestamp (e.g. `2026-01-31T14:30:00Z`).

Returns entities created or updated after this timestamp and is intended for incremental synchronization.
Combine with delete webhooks for full synchronization.

CustomProperties.name: custom_properties
CustomProperties.description:
Filter by custom field values.

Unknown custom field names return an empty result set. For MultiSelect fields,
pass multiple values using `custom_properties[Field][]=A&custom_properties[Field][]=B`.
Boolean fields should be queried with `true` or `false`.

Link.description:
RFC 5988 Web Linking header for pagination.
Contains a link to the next page with `rel="next"` if more pages are available.
Example: `<https://demo.mocoapp.com/api/v1/projects?page=4>; rel="next"`

BadRequest.description: Bad request. Check the error message in the response body for details.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized. Check the error message in the response body and verify your API key.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden. Check your Authentication or your MOCO user permission.

NotFound.description: Not found. Check that the resource exists (maybe it was deleted in the meantime).

UnprocessableEntity.description: Validation failed. Check the provided error message in the response body.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests. You can expect to be able to send 120 requests per 2 minutes (~1 request per second). For the unlimited plan, it is 1200 requests per 2 minutes (~10 per second). If you exceed this limit, the server responds with this status code.
